newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil says no new telephone rate plan decided yet.
newsitem.headline: Brazil says no new telephone rate plan decided yet.

text.p: Brazil's Communications Ministry said it has not yet set a schedule for a new round of phone rate adjustments to eliminate subsidies ahead of the privatization of the state's telecoms monopoly Telebras.
"There's no decision yet. We have no schedule, no percentages," ministry spokesman Francisco Mendonca told Reuters. "We haven't even finished our study yet."
Local television quoted Telebras President Fernando Xavier, who spoke before Congress' lower house on Wednesday, as saying phone call rates will rise 200 percent in a second round of adjustments.
Both the ministry and Telebras strongly denied the report.
"When I heard that on the news, I nearly fell out of my chair," Mendonca said. "I couldn't believe it. He said nothing like that."
The report has stirred up added confusion about Brazil's plans to restructure telecommunications tariffs to prepare the sector for increased competition as Telebras is privatized in coming years.

In August, press reports that Xavier expected a 200 percent hike in the basic residential subscription rate generated confusion in financial markets and sparked a jump in Telebras shares in Sao Paulo and New York.
The shares drop back after officials denied the reports, but the markets are understandably sensitive to possible changes in phone rates.

Last November's first round of adjustments has prompted Telebras profits and its shares to soar this year. The company's preferred share is the Sao Paulo bourse's benchmark and trades as in New York as an American Depositary Receipt.
But the controversy has fueled suspicion among stock traders and in the press.

Local business magazine CartaCapital asserted in its Oct 16 edition that Communications Minister Sergio Motta and Telebras officials have manipulated Telebras stock with comments on everything from tariffs to privatization.
Both the company and the ministry deny this. "That's absurd," Mendonca said. "Anyone who's followed the issue closely knows that's not true."
A Telebras spokesman also vehemently denied Xavier has ever given figures about a rate hike, adding the press misreported his comments in August and TV Globo repeated the mistake this week.
Rate changes are drafted and approved by the communications and finance ministries, not Telebras, he added.
Stock market analysts interviewed by Reuters expect an initial round of rate adjustments in late December or early in 1997, roughly coinciding with the anniversary of a first round in late 1995.

They predict the basic residential subscription rate of 3.74 reais will rise between 50 percent and 90 percent and local call rates 10 percent to 60 percent from the current level 0.05 reais per three minutes. International rates should fall between five and 10 percent, they added.
